questions.question: What does ifPresent() do in an Optional?
options: Executes a Consumer if the Optional has a value
Returns the value of the Optional
Creates a new Optional with the transformed value
Throws an exception if it is empty
explanations: Correct. ifPresent(consumer) executes the Consumer action only if the Optional contains a value.
To return the value you use get() or orElse().
To transform you use map().
To throw an exception you use orElseThrow().

questions.question: What does map() do in an Optional?
options: Transforms the value if it exists, returning an Optional with the new value
Filters the value according to a condition
Flattens nested Optionals
Returns the value or a default
explanations: Correct. map(function) applies the transformation to the value of the Optional if it exists, returning a new Optional.
To filter you use filter().
To flatten you use flatMap().
For a value or default you use orElse().

questions.question: What does flatMap() do in an Optional?
options: Transforms the value avoiding the creation of a nested Optional (Optional<Optional<T>>)
Returns the value or a default
Filters null values
Executes an action if there is a value
explanations: Correct. flatMap(function) applies a function that returns an Optional, avoiding Optional<Optional<T>>.
For a value or default you use orElse().
To filter you use filter().
To execute an action you use ifPresent().

questions.question: What does orElseThrow() do in an Optional?
options: Returns the value if it exists or throws an exception if the Optional is empty
Always returns null
Ignores the value and returns void
Creates a new empty Optional
explanations: Correct. orElseThrow() returns the value if it is present or throws NoSuchElementException (or a custom exception) if it is empty.
It does not return null.
It does not return void.
It does not create an empty Optional.

questions.question: Why is it recommended not to use get() directly on an Optional?
options: Because it throws NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty
Because it returns null
Because it is slower than orElse()
Because get() does not exist in Optional
explanations: Correct. get() throws NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty, so orElse(), orElseThrow(), or ifPresent() are preferred.
It does not return null.
It is not a matter of performance.
get() does exist in Optional.
